result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers are fully in Spanish, give an honest description of the weekly newsletter, offer a neutral 'No, gracias', invent no benefits and mention unsubscribing at any time. Answer B is a cleaner two-button pop-up that thanks the customer for the order, adds practical GDPR advice (closing with the X counts as 'No', keep a record of consent), and speaks directly to the goal of getting more sign-ups without pressure. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are fully in Spanish, invent no incentives and mention that people can unsubscribe. A gives a clean pop-up: a title, a thank-you plus a weekly-content line, and two equally weighted buttons. Its advice is practical and speaks to the owner's goal of getting more sign-ups without pressure. B adds an unticked checkbox on top of the Subscribe/No buttons, which is redundant and confusing (what happens if someone clicks Subscribe without ticking it?), so A is the cleaner deliverable.
